content.title: About
content.content: Fried flounder is a tender fillet of flounder coated in breadcrumbs or a seasoned batter and fried until golden and crisp. The fish has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a delicate texture, while the coating adds a crunchy exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flounder is a flat, bottom‑dwelling fish found in coastal waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
It can change its coloration to blend with the sea floor, making it a master of camouflage.
Flounder fillets are low in fat but rich in protein and omega‑3 fatty acids.
Traditionally, fried flounder is served with lemon wedges and fresh herbs.
In some cuisines the breading includes spices such as paprika, garlic, and parsley.

items.title: Rich in high‑quality protein
items.content: Flounder provides complete proteins essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health and help reduce inflammation.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The low saturated‑fat content makes it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Contains vitamins D and B12
items.content: Vitamin D aids bone health, while B12 is important for nerve function and blood formation.

items.title: Provides minerals like selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, and phosphorus is vital for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to fish, including flounder, and should avoid it.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: As with other marine fish, flounder may contain trace amounts of heavy metals; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: High sodium in processed versions
items.content: Pre‑breaded products often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options when possible.

items.title: Cooking oil quality
items.content: Use oil with a high smoke point for frying to prevent formation of harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried flounder hot, typically with a lemon wedge, fresh herbs, or a light sauce. It pairs well with mashed potatoes, vegetable sides, or a simple green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fried flounder in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
